description: Install a plugin from a local source directory at runtime and bring its entry-point online without restarting the solet. The verb validates the path exists, is a directory, and contains either plugin.yaml or pyproject.toml (refuses otherwise). Before running pip at all, it refuses with a structured error if the plugin name already exists in this environment — either already loaded in the live roster, or installed (entry-point present) but not loaded (an inert connector awaiting a blue-green boot) — because a same-name pip install cannot safely replace either without risking the existing distribution; the caller is pointed to apply_manifest (blue-green) for both cases. Once past that guard it runs `pip install -e <path>` against the active Python interpreter via subprocess, then stages a single new plugin class (entry-point discovery scoped to just its name), wires it (orchestrator_ref and event_bus injected before prepare_for_readiness, then initialize and start_services), and commits it into the live roster with one atomic dict store via the plugin manager's single-plugin installer. The new plugin is the only roster entry touched — every other already-loaded plugin's instance is untouched, and a failure at any staging phase (contract validation, wiring) or at the post-commit registry refresh rolls the just-installed pip artifact back and leaves the whole roster, allowlist, and every pre-existing instance byte-identical. On a successful install, the new plugin's process keys are collected from its get_available_actions and pushed into the registry via knowledge_service::refresh_plugin_processes so they become immediately invocable; a completed envelope always carries installed=true — there is no success-with-installed=false outcome, only the distinct error cases above. The pip subprocess inherits the active venv automatically (sys.executable -m pip). Refuses with a structured error if pip exits non-zero, surfacing the captured stderr so the caller can diagnose dependency conflicts.
embedding_description: Install a plugin from a local path at runtime. pip install -e a plugin source directory. Bring a freshly-checked-out plugin online without restarting the solet. Add a new plugin entry-point to the live orchestrator. Install a sibling plugin from a workbench scratch directory. Hot install a Python package as a solet plugin and register its process keys.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Install result with keys: installed (bool, always true on a completed envelope — a same-name plugin that already exists, loaded or not, is refused as a distinct error before pip runs, never returned as a false/success value), plugin_name (str, name of the newly installed plugin), new_process_keys (list[str] of process keys the new plugin contributes), message (str status detail).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: On a successful install, confirm the plugin name and surface the new_process_keys count. If pip failed, surface the captured stderr verbatim so the caller can read the dependency conflict or build error. If the error names the plugin as already loaded or already installed-but-not-loaded, say so explicitly and point to apply_manifest — pip never ran in that case, so there is no artifact to roll back.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: On installed=true, the new plugin's process keys are immediately invocable; the next step can call them. If the error says the plugin is already loaded or already installed but not loaded, do not retry install — use apply_manifest + the bound self_deployment_service plugin so the roster picks up the new bytecode via blue-green instead. If the install succeeded but the plugin did not appear in the roster, check the package's pyproject.toml for an [project.entry-points."ananta.plugins"] block.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Install a plugin from a local directory via pip install -e and bring its entry-point online
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: ValidationError: path was empty, did not exist, was not a directory, or contained neither plugin.yaml nor pyproject.toml. PluginManagerUnavailable: the orchestrator's plugin_manager attribute is missing. AlreadyLoaded: the plugin name is already in the live roster — pip never ran; a same-name re-install cannot replace a live instance. AlreadyInstalledNotLoaded: the plugin's entry-point already exists in this environment (e.g. an inert connector staged for a blue-green boot) but is not in the live roster — pip never ran; re-installing could not safely replace the existing distribution. PipInstallFailure: the pip subprocess exited non-zero — the captured stderr is in the error message; common causes are dependency conflicts, build errors, or a malformed pyproject.toml. PluginInstallError at phase=staging_discovery/contract_validation/wiring: pip succeeded but the staged plugin failed discovery, contract validation, or lifecycle wiring (prepare_for_readiness/initialize/start_services) — the just-installed pip artifact is rolled back and the live roster is untouched. A post-commit registry-refresh failure (missing/unusable knowledge_service, or the refresh reporting errors) unwinds the same way: pip artifact rolled back, roster untouched, reported as an install failure naming the registry-refresh cause.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For path errors: ensure the directory exists and contains plugin.yaml or pyproject.toml. For AlreadyLoaded or AlreadyInstalledNotLoaded: do not retry install_plugin_from_path — use apply_manifest + the bound self_deployment_service plugin (blue-green) to bring the new code online instead. For PipInstallFailure: read the stderr and resolve the underlying pip error before retrying; if the build needs system dependencies, install them first. For PluginInstallError at any phase, or a registry-refresh failure: the pip artifact was already rolled back and the roster is untouched, so it is safe to fix the underlying cause (missing dependency, contract mismatch, a raise in prepare_for_readiness/initialize, or the registry-refresh error named in the message) and retry install_plugin_from_path from scratch.
